div.head: Norðleoda 1
div.ab: Cynges wergild is inne mid Englum on folcriht XXX þusend þrymsa: XV þusend þrymsa byð þæs weres 7 XV þusend þæs cynedomes; se wer gebyreð þam magum 7 seo cynebot þam leodum.

Regis weregildum est cum Anglis in (iure) publico recto XXX milia þrimsa: id est XV milia þrimsa sunt de wera et XV milia cynedomes, id est regie dignitatis (censure); ipsum natalis eius pretium pertinet cognationi et cynebot ipsius terrę nationi.
Norðleoda cynges gild is XXX þusend þrymsa: fiftene þusend þrymsa bið þæs wergildes, XV þusend þæs cynedomes; se wer gebirað magum 7 seo cynebot þam leodum.
Be wergylde Cynges wergild is inne mid Englum on folcriht XXX þusend þrymsa: XV þusend ðrymsa byð þæs weres and XV þusend þæs cynedomes; se wer gebyreð þam magum and seo cynebot þam leodum.

The payment for a king of the North people is 30,000 thrymsas; 15,000 thrymsas belong to the wergild, 15,000 to the kingship; the wergild belongs to the kinsmen and the royal-compensation to the people.

According to the folk law of the English people, a king’s wergild is thirty thousand thrymsas: fifteen thousand thrymsas are for the man and fifteen thousand thrymsas are for the kingship. The personal wergild belongs to his kinsmen and the royal compensation belongs to the people.

Entgelt (Wergeld hlq) für den König der Nordleute ist volksrechtlich [im Lande H] (bei den Engländern hlq) 30 000 Tremissen [375 Pfund]: (und von denen seien Ld) 15 000 Tremissen ist [Betrag] des Wergeldes (und) 15 000 [der] der Königswürde; das Wergeld gebührt den Verwandten (gehört der Sippe des Königsgeschlechts Ld) und die Königsbusse dem Volke (des Landes lq).

The payment (wergild, hlq) for the king of the North-people is by folk-right [in the land, H] (among the English, hlq) 30,000 thrymsas [375 pounds]: (and of these let there be, Ld) 15,000 thrymsas [as the sum] of the wergild (and) 15,000 [that] of the kingship; the wergild belongs to the kinsmen (belongs to the kin of the royal house, Ld) and the king-compensation to the people (of the land, lq).
div.note: H's ‘inne mid Englum’ is a corruption in hlq (compare Grið 4). D supplies ‘on folcriht’ from the others and Mirce 3. Liebermann compares Mirce 3.1 and 4.
id. replaces “North people” with “by folk-law among the English”.
One thryms is equal to three pennies.
Cynges: Norðleoda cynges D inne . . . folcriht: omitted D weres: wergildes D þam magum: þam omitted D

[title] On Wergild: The earlier version of the Compilation titles this text The Law of the Northern People. A major component of Wulfstan’s revision was to diminish the regional specificity of the individual texts, though this should not be taken as a sign that the wergild values listed here necessarily applied south of the Humber.

a king’s wergild: Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 201 reads, “The wergild of a king of the northern people.” thrymsas: The term “thrymsa” was used both as a general term for coins and more specifically as the equivalent of one-third of a shilling, about four pennies. It is the latter meaning which most likely applies here.
